  node.ts ("villanelle/node"): createFsLoader(): DocumentLoader; createFsWriter(): IDocumentWriter
  browser.ts ("villanelle/browser"): interface IFetchWriterOptions { method?: string; contentType?: string }; createFetchLoader(fetchImpl: typeof fetch): DocumentLoader; createFetchWriter(fetchImpl: typeof fetch, options?: IFetchWriterOptions): IDocumentWriter
Renames from the reference (new package, no aliases): parse -> parseGraph, IParseConfig -> IParseGraphOptions, DocumentWriter -> IDocumentWriter (STYLE 3.6). IDocumentNode holds the facade (`document`) instead of parseResult/cst/ast; the syntax is document.syntax.

BEHAVIOUR (reference parse.ts unless stated)
1. An include is a directive named "include" anywhere in a document (blocks included). Its first arg must be a STRING (arg.value().kind === 'string'; vil-bgz: include paths are quoted); otherwise E2006 and no edge. The spec is the decoded string.
2. Loader errors: an empty result -> E3001, edge with no targets; a rejection -> E3004 (message includes the error's message), edge with no targets.
3. Matches are sorted by resolvedPath with compareCodePoints (vil-bgz.1); createFsLoader sorts its glob matches with the same helper. compareCodePoints compares by Unicode code point (so it agrees with Python's str order), never localeCompare or UTF-16 `<`.
4. A document already in the graph is parsed once and reused. A cycle (a target still being processed) gives E3002 and the edge targets that open node. Depth: the root is 0; an include whose targets would sit deeper than maxIncludeDepth (default 16) gives E3003 and an edge with no targets. CHANGE from the reference: no empty stand-in document is added to `nodes`.
5. Include diagnostics (E2006, E3001-E3004) carry the include directive's span and the resolvedPath of the document that contains the include. CHANGE from the reference, which used a 0:0 span and, for cycles and depth, the target's path. Each document's syntax diagnostics are added with that document's resolvedPath when it is parsed. Order: as found (see the docblock).
6. A missing loader throws TypeError whose message contains "loader is required" (the ported test's regex).
7. composeLoaders, iterateDirectives and save: as the reference and the docblocks. iterateDirectives keeps the reference order (a directive, then its body; an include replaced by its targets' directives); vil-bgz owns the nesting-preserving view.
8. node.ts: specs resolve against dirname(parentPath); a glob (* or ?) only in the last path segment lists that directory (files only) and returns matches sorted with compareCodePoints; a missing non-glob file rejects. browser.ts: as the reference.

ACCEPTANCE -> TEST: reference include.test.ts ported (single, nested, missing, cycle, depth, multiple glob matches, ordering, no matches, loader failure, missing loader) and green; a code-point order test with mixed case, accented and astral paths asserts the exact order; diagnostics carry the include's span and resolvedPath; a node.ts test against a temp dir (os.tmpdir(), a few bytes) covers a glob; `corepack pnpm -C ts build` succeeds and `node -e "import('villanelle/node')"` and "villanelle/browser" resolve from ts/ (package self-reference).

Not owned: ts/src/diagnostics.ts. The 15 codes are frozen; if the classifier needs a code that is not there, or cannot emit one that is, stop and return an erratum.

FROZEN SURFACE: no new public symbol. parse(text): ISyntax keeps its signature and gains these guarantees: total for every input, depth.json included (never throws); every token in exactly one place (each token index is either directly in one node's range and in no child, or inside exactly one child), for valid and broken input.
Private contract inside ts/src/syntax/ (the internal seam; free to refine as long as it stays private):
  export const MAX_NESTING = 100;
  export interface IRawDiagnostic { readonly code: DiagnosticCode; readonly range: ITokenRange; readonly message: string }  // token range; empty at end of input
  export function installRecovery(parser: VillanelleParser, report: (diagnostic: IRawDiagnostic) => void): void;
parse.ts stays the one place that turns token ranges into ISourceSpan (spanOf).

BEHAVIOUR
1. Port design/experiments/v4/antlr/ts/recovery.ts (custom DefaultErrorStrategy: sync is a no-op, recoverInline never conjures a token, skip to the end of the bad statement) and the entry.ts override getSynValidOrSemInvalidAltThatFinishedDecisionEntryRule = () => 0, so the first error is reported at its real position.
2. A bad statement becomes one error node and later siblings are kept (owner, vil-bzv.3).
3. Code classifier, first match wins, by offending token t (port of reportError): BAD_CHAR, or BOM at index > 0 -> E1003; UNTERMINATED_STRING -> E1001; inside a slice bracket -> E2007; t is ']' or (inside a list bracket and t is '}' or end of input) -> E2004; t is '{' that starts its line (only spaces/comments before it on the line) -> E2008; end of input inside a block -> E2003; t is a WORD, STRING or '[' that touches the previous value (the token right before t, with no SPACE or COMMENT between, is a WORD, STRING or a ']' that closes a value) -> E2009; otherwise E2001. Lift the classifier into a pure function so the Python port copies it line for line.
4. Depth guard, before the parser runs: one pass over the tokens counting open '{' and '[' (closing tokens decrement, never below 0). If the count ever exceeds MAX_NESTING, the parser is not run: root = document [0, n) with exactly one child, an error node [0, n), and diagnostics = [one E2010 at the '{' or '[' that opens level 101]. title: config: open-source packaging and spec
description: plans/nextgen.md milestone 0 and API hygiene: RASL-centric name/README/fixtures; parseDocument (sync single-file) not exported so the simplest use needs async parse plus a dummy loader; public types mutable; no published grammar. Interface naming follows js/STYLE.md 3.6 (I prefix kept).
design: Confirmed language rules (nextgen §Current decisions): newline ends a directive; semicolons optional, needed only for several directives on one line. No backslash line continuation. Newlines allowed inside [...] lists until the matching ']'. '{' on the same line as its header. Strings use ' or ". v1 escapes: \\ \n \t \r \" \' only. Comments: // and /* */ only (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Dot is part of a word. Unquoted words: letters, digits, underscores, dots, no hyphens (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Diagnostics: 0-based line/column, stable codes plus messages. Public API keeps the directive-level AST; no RASL node/connection AST. Core does no I/O. Spec deliverables: EBNF grammar plus lexical spec; versioned core profile; conformance corpus of inputs with expected tokens/CST/diagnostics as JSON. Milestone 0: generic README, RASL examples move to the consumer, neutral fixtures (e.g. server { listen 8080; }). Spec states the unit of offset and column.
acceptance_criteria: RASL removed from package surface; a sync single-file parse entry point exported; public types readonly; the grammar epic's spec is published with the package.

title: config: AST editing API with token splicing
description: README claims AST edits modify the CST, but IAstDirective has no mutators and the token-splice utilities in plans/roundtrip.md do not exist, so save() has nothing to persist. No consumer needs editing yet; fix the README claim now.
design: Confirmed (nextgen, roundtrip): byte-identical serializeCst(parse(x).cst) === x is first-class. Trivia kept in CST. Canonical storage is the full token stream; directive nodes reference token ranges, never copy tokens. Tokens keep raw text and 0-based spans. Serialization is token concatenation; subtree = node's token range. Edits are token splices keeping spans stable; no trivia-attachment heuristics. Three tiers: power users edit tokens/CST byte-identically; most use the AST facade (edits may normalize formatting); minimal consumers use declarative registration (vil-xlo). Tests: golden round-trip; mutation tests assert only intended token ranges change.
